from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A basis defines your coordinate grid.", "Robby sees the world differently.", "Different grids, same point."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift", lecture_lines)

        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5})
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        vec_v = Arrow(ORIGIN, [1, 2, 0], color="#3498DB")
        vec_v.next_to(grid.c2p(0,0), UP, buff=0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(vec_v))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3498DB")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#E74C3C")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Any vector is a linear combination.", "Summing basis vectors reaches any point.", "Coordinates are weights of the basis."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis and Linear Combinations", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 6], y_range=[-1, 6], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.4)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F")
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color="#F1C40F")
        
        v = Vector([3, 2], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        # Vector summation: v = 3*i + 2*j
        i1 = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=LEFT)
        i2 = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(1, 0), aligned_edge=LEFT)
        i3 = Vector([1, 0], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(2, 0), aligned_edge=LEFT)
        j1 = Vector([0, 1], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(3, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        j2 = Vector([0, 1], color="#F1C40F").move_to(axes.c2p(3, 1), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(i1), Create(i2), Create(i3), Create(j1), Create(j2))
        self.play(Create(v))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        
        v_label = MathTex(r"v = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}", color="#2ECC71").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "A3")
        
        self.play(Write(v_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We need a transition matrix P.",
            "P maps old to new basis.",
            "Represent coordinates in a new grid.",
            "P columns are the old basis.",
            "Formula: v_old equals P times v_new."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Change of Basis Matrix (P)", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Mobjects ---
        matrix_P = MathTex(r"P = \begin{bmatrix} a & c \\ b & d \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        vector_v_new = MathTex(r"v_{new} = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        mult_expr = MathTex(r"P \cdot v_{new}", color="#9B59B6")
        formula = MathTex(r"v_{old} = P \cdot v_{new}", color=WHITE)
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_P, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(matrix_P))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.place_at_grid(mult_expr, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(mult_expr))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.place_at_grid(vector_v_new, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(vector_v_new))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 4 ---
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        # Highlight columns of P
        self.play(matrix_P.animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 5 ---
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        formula.set_color("#F1C40F")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "E3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Step one, identify the new basis.", "Step two, construct the matrix P.", "Step three, multiply by your coordinates.", "Color-coded columns guide the process.", "Now your point is re-represented."]

        eq_mult = MathTex(r"P \cdot \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix}").scale(0.8)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Synthesis & Wrap-up", [
            "Changing basis simplifies complex problems.",
            "Symmetry aligns with your calculation axis.",
            "Diagonal matrices make physics easy."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show summary graphic (abstract representation of a basis change)
        basis_viz = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP * 2, color=WHITE)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(basis_viz, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(basis_viz), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate transition from abstract (original basis) to concrete (aligned with symmetry)
        rot_angle = PI/4
        basis_viz_rotated = basis_viz.copy().rotate(rot_angle, about_point=basis_viz.get_center())
        basis_viz_rotated.set_color(GREEN)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(basis_viz.copy(), basis_viz_rotated), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#3498DB"), run_time=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display concluding text (Diagonal matrices make physics easy)
        diag_matrix = Matrix([[3, 0], [0, 5]], h_buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(diag_matrix, 'E4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(diag_matrix), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift
sections.content: Define 'Basis' as a coordinate system (a grid). Use an animation of a robot (Robby) standing in a 2D plane. Show that the same point in space can be described by different coordinate values depending on which grid (basis) Robby uses.
sections.example: Robby the Robot: Position (2, 3) in a standard grid vs. position (1, 1) in a tilted, stretched grid.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis and Linear Combinations
sections.content: Quickly recap that any vector v can be expressed as a unique linear combination of basis vectors: v = c1*b1 + c2*b2. Use a visual 'Vector Summation' animation where two arrows (basis vectors) are stacked head-to-tail to reach a target point.
sections.example: Representing vector v = [5, 7] as 5 times the unit vector 'i' plus 7 times the unit vector 'j'.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (P)
sections.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix P. Explain that P stores the old basis vectors expressed in terms of the new basis vectors as its columns. Provide the formula: [v]old = P * [v]new.
sections.example: A transformation matrix P that converts coordinates from a 'Standard Grid' to a 'Camera View' for a character in a game engine.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Computational Workflow
sections.content: Demonstrate the algorithm: 1. Identify the new basis vectors. 2. Construct the matrix P. 3. Multiply P by the coordinate vector to get the new representation. Visual aid: Use color-coded columns to show how basis vectors map into the matrix.
sections.example: Converting a coordinate from Basis B = { (1,0), (0,1) } to Basis B' = { (1,1), (-1,1) }.

sections.title: Real-World Synthesis & Wrap-up
sections.content: Conclude with an application: Why do we do this? It simplifies complex problems! Briefly show a physics simulation where changing the basis to align with an object's symmetry axis turns a difficult calculation into a simple diagonal matrix.
sections.example: A spinning propeller: Changing the basis to align with the blade's rotation axis to simplify the force vector calculations.
